place: a chemistry lab in Bologna
who: a first-year student named Matteo and the lab assistant
situation: Matteo arrives in flip-flops for his first lab class. The assistant points to a yellow sign about closed shoes and safety glasses.

place: a quiet university library in Kyoto
who: two graduate students, Kenji and Yuna
situation: Someone left a warm cup of green tea and an open laptop at the corner desk, yet nobody comes back for forty minutes.

place: a campus exam room in Manchester
who: an older history student named Priya
situation: Priya spends three nights learning dates for a test, then reads on the front page that students only answer two of six parts.

place: a student dorm kitchen in Warsaw
who: three roommates, Piotr, Samira, and Leo
situation: The smoke alarm rings at midnight and a black pan sits in the sink, though nobody admits cooking a late snack.

place: a biology professor's office in Cape Town
who: a tired university student named Thabo and Dr. Patel
situation: Thabo waited until Sunday night to write his ten-page paper, and his laptop battery died before he saved the last draft.

place: a language testing center in Seoul
who: a test supervisor and forty applicants
situation: A printed guide explains how to turn off smartwatches, leave bags in lockers, and show a photo ID before entering the room.

place: an old campus cafe in Salamanca
who: a retired librarian named Carmen and her granddaughter
situation: Carmen walks past the new tablet desks and remembers when students waited in line for paper book cards and noisy typewriters.

place: a noisy college study room in Montreal
who: two classmates, Bastien and Zainab
situation: Zainab forgot her calculator before the math quiz, and Bastien has an extra solar one sitting at the bottom of his backpack.

place: an architecture studio in Helsinki
who: a second-year student named Olli and his tutor
situation: Olli wants to use the wood workshop after 8 p.m., which requires a green pass from the afternoon safety class.

place: a crowded university hall in Buenos Aires
who: an exam monitor and a law student named Sofia
situation: Halfway through the final exam, Sofia's phone plays a loud salsa ringtone from inside her jacket pocket on the floor.

place: an open-plan design office in Berlin
who: an office manager named Lukas and twelve designers
situation: Someone heated smoked fish in the small breakroom microwave, so Lukas sends a firm message about kitchen rules before lunch.

place: a busy accounting office in Nairobi
who: a junior clerk named Amina and her team lead
situation: Amina checks the office bike rack at 7:30 a.m. and sees her manager's red bicycle already locked outside in the rain.

place: a small book publisher in Dublin
who: an editor named Ciara and a new intern
situation: The intern prints eighty color copies of the weekly schedule, not knowing the team moved to a shared online calendar last month.

place: a shared office space in Lisbon
who: two freelance programmers, Diego and Mei
situation: Diego needs a quiet booth for a client call, and Mei offers to watch his bag and lend him her spare charger.

place: a shipping office in Rotterdam
who: a warehouse planner named Bram and the IT desk
situation: A huge price spreadsheet disappeared overnight, and Bram sees an unknown login from the night shift computer at 2 a.m.

place: a local newspaper office in Melbourne
who: a senior photographer named Ravi and a young reporter
situation: Over coffee, Ravi talks about the years when everyone worked late in a darkroom printing paper photos before the morning paper.

place: a customer support center in Manila
who: a shift supervisor named Marisol and new staff
situation: Company policy lets workers stay home two days a week once they finish their first ninety days of office training.

place: a dental clinic front desk in Zurich
who: a receptionist named Ingrid and a tired assistant
situation: The assistant forgot to lock the filing drawer and left a patient's paper appointment card sitting upside down near the printer.

place: a rooftop terrace at a tech office in Austin
who: a marketing planner named Farah and her coworker
situation: Farah skipped the Friday team lunch to finish slides early, then heard the meeting moved to Tuesday and free tacos arrived.

place: a city bus office in Prague
who: a building safety officer and forty office workers
situation: A poster next to the elevator explains where to stand outside during the monthly fire drill and why hallways stay empty.

place: a hotel lobby in Singapore
who: a young cook named Jin and a head chef
situation: Jin spills coffee on his white shirt ten minutes before his kitchen interview, and the front desk has a clean apron.

place: a small bakery in Lyon
who: a shop owner named Claire and a teenage applicant
situation: The morning job starts at 4:30 a.m. to bake bread, yet the applicant admits he sleeps through three loud alarms.

place: a bright glass meeting room in Toronto
who: two hiring managers, Sanjay and Greta
situation: An applicant left the interview smiling and brought three strong reference letters, so the managers think he led a sales team before.

place: a quiet bedroom in Cairo
who: a graphic designer named Tarek
situation: Tarek wore a full suit and tie for his video interview, then saw the hiring manager wearing a hoodie and holding a cat.

place: a career center in Glasgow
who: a job coach named Fiona and a recent graduate
situation: The graduate emailed the same cover letter to twelve companies with the wrong company name still written in the first line.

place: an animal clinic in Santiago
who: a vet named Beatriz and an applicant named Hugo
situation: Hugo sits in the waiting room and hears two dogs barking behind the closed door, guessing the clinic is very busy today.

place: a local radio station in Lagos
who: a station producer named Chidi and a young volunteer
situation: Before becoming a sound engineer, Chidi spent five summers fixing broken speakers and carrying heavy cables for neighborhood street bands.

place: a company job website in Stockholm
who: a software company's HR team and applicants
situation: The online application guide tells applicants not to add photos or birth dates, and to upload only a plain two-page resume.

place: a coffee shop near a bank in Frankfurt
who: an accountant named Viktor and his sister
situation: Viktor said no to a remote job offer last spring because the office looked small, and now that company doubled its pay.

place: a city flower garden in Wellington
who: a park manager named Aroha and a new gardener
situation: After passing the greenhouse test, the new gardener receives a brass key and gets access to the rare orchid room alone.

place: an apartment hallway in Madrid
who: a teacher named Elena and a delivery driver
situation: Elena ordered a tall wooden bookshelf online, yet the tiny cardboard box at her door clearly holds a dollhouse toy.

place: a busy electronics store in Osaka
who: a shopper named Hiroshi and a sales clerk
situation: Hiroshi wants to return wireless headphones without the box, and the clerk points to the return rule printed on the receipt.

place: a neighborhood post office in Vienna
who: a retired baker named Otto and a counter clerk
situation: Otto carries a heavy parcel tied with brown string, and the clerk offers to tape the corners and print an address sticker.

place: a clothes shop in Milan
who: a shopper named Nadia and a shop assistant
situation: A silver sign outside the fitting rooms reminds shoppers to bring only three items inside and leave coffee cups on the shelf.

place: a home kitchen in Chicago
who: a dad named Marcus and his teenage daughter
situation: Marcus paid extra for next-day shipping on a birthday blender, then found out the shop two blocks away had it on sale.

place: a local farmers market in Oaxaca
who: a fruit seller named Rosa and a visitor
situation: Rosa remembers when every shopper carried woven baskets and paid in coins, long before card machines sat beside the mango boxes.

place: a shoe shop help chat in Amsterdam
who: a customer named Lotte and a support agent
situation: Lotte's parcel tracking shows it sitting in one warehouse for six days, and the agent suspects the address label fell off.

place: a second-hand bike shop in Copenhagen
who: a mechanic named Astrid and a college student
situation: The student bought a cheap helmet online with a cracked strap, so Astrid explains how to check safety labels before paying.

place: a large supermarket in Kuala Lumpur
who: a cashier named Nurul and a regular shopper
situation: The store's new phone app lets members scan groceries themselves and skip the long checkout line on busy Sunday afternoons.

place: an old music shop in Athens
who: a collector named Nikos and the shop owner
situation: Nikos left a rare jazz record on the counter to get cash from a bank machine, and someone else bought it quickly.

place: an airport security line in Istanbul
who: a passenger named Kerem and a security officer
situation: Kerem packed a big glass jar of homemade olive oil in his hand bag, forgetting the strict liquid limit at security.

place: a departure gate in Bangkok
who: two backpackers, Ananya and Liam
situation: The boarding screen suddenly turns green and flight staff wave passengers forward, so Ananya thinks their late plane finally arrived.

place: a narrow train carriage near Florence
who: an older traveler named Giorgio and a student
situation: Giorgio struggles to lift his heavy green suitcase onto the high shelf while the train begins rolling out of the station.

place: a small ferry port in Reykjavik
who: a tour guide named Jonas and twelve tourists
situation: Dark clouds roll over the harbor and the wind shakes the ticket booth, so Jonas warns everyone to put on warm raincoats.

place: a noisy baggage hall in Mexico City
who: a business traveler named Valeria
situation: Everyone else from the flight already left with their bags, and only one scratched pink suitcase circles the empty belt alone.

place: a budget airline desk in Edinburgh
who: a student named Kofi and a gate agent
situation: Kofi paid to print three paper copies of his boarding pass at a hotel desk, then saw everyone scanning phones at the gate.

place: an airport lounge in Doha
who: a flight attendant named Leila and a tired passenger
situation: Passengers with a wait longer than eight hours between flights get free entry to the quiet shower rooms and a hot meal coupon.

place: a passport control hall in Porto
who: an airport officer and arriving travelers
situation: Blue signs above the electronic gates tell travelers to take off hats and sunglasses and hold passports flat on the glass scanner.

place: a mountain bus station in Cusco
who: a bus driver named Esteban and a young hiker
situation: Esteban points to the smooth new road and remembers when dusty wooden buses took nine bumpy hours to climb the same hill.

place: an airport shuttle stop in Vancouver
who: a musician named Hana and a taxi driver
situation: Hana booked a cheap 5 a.m. flight to save twenty dollars, then paid sixty dollars for a taxi after missing the bus.
